Proactive Service Agents: A Unified Decision
Framework, Methods, and Evaluation
Yan Tang, Tingyu Cao, Yuanbo Tang, Huaze Tang, and Keer Hu
Abstract—Large language model agents can plan, invoke tools,
and modify external states, yet most systems still take an explicit
user instruction as a fixed starting point. Proactive service moves
the decision upstream: an agent must infer service opportunities
from incomplete environmental and user signals, choose among
remaining silent, asking, assisting, and acting, and account for
interruption, misunderstanding, overreach, and privacy costs.
This survey gives an operational definition centered on initiative
and formulates the problem as a partially observable sequential
decision process constrained by authorization and risk. The
formulation represents timing, content, and delivery within one
structured action, while making explicit the option

proactive
decision.
Definition 1(Proactive service intervention).A non-silent
action at at time t is aproactive service interventionrelative
to ιt if: (i) the system autonomously introduces at least one
service opportunity, trigger time, service subgoal, information-
acquisition action, or commitment to an external action
not entailed by ιt; (ii) the protocol permits silence, direct
completion of the specified task, or another feasible action;
(iii) the system selects the action from beliefs about the user's
objective, the environment, and the consequences; and (iv) the
objective includes user-endorsed benefit or shared task benefit.
Choosing wording, a search path, or implementation details for
already requested content is not itself a proactive intervention.

A. Three Regimes Share the Same Decision Variables
Applications need not create another domain catalog. Ta-
ble IV organizes work into three deployment regimes by obser-
vation continuity, time window, action reversibility, permission,
and feedback delay. The threshold and admissible set of the
same method change systematically across regimes.
In digital workspaces, a richer act set is appropriate when
actions are sandboxed and tested, their impact can be previewed,
and external side effects can be rolled back. Continuous screen
capture nevertheless exposes information unrelated to the task,
and reversibility is not costlessness. Software-engineering clari-
fication shows that detecting underspecification, asking a useful
question, and exploiting the answer are distinct bottlenecks [66],
[56]. In contextual and embodied environments, timing and
perception errors are coupled: late help

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: No blocking reasons: the manuscript's scoped survey contribution, formal decision framework, critical evaluation protocol, and explicit limitation handling are well supported by the supplied evidence.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Theoretical formulations and survey claims are well aligned; the authors explicitly avoid overclaiming empirical deployment benefit, clarifying where existing benchmarks are limited to static constructed cases (R0) or offline replays (R1) without closed-loop intervention dynamics.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The paper provides a structured critical analysis of existing benchmarks across modalities by establishing a standardized decision-unit schema and evaluating studies via an orthogonal three-axis evidence descriptor (interaction realism, comparison design, and human-outcome horizon). It rigorously formalizes metrics for gating calibration, event-level timing precision/recall, and off-policy/counterfactual evaluation.
primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate the limitations of current literature, emphasizing that high failure-prediction or classification F1 does not imply real-world deployment utility, and outlining open challenges regarding counterfactual evaluation, preference drift, and multi-regime protocol harmonization.
primary.method_assessment: The manuscript establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation using a constrained POMDP formulation with separate state beliefs and verifiable permission ledgers, decomposes actions into structured modes (silent, ask, assist, act), and defines the incremental intervention advantage over waiting while analyzing single-crossing threshold conditions.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript satisfies all standards for a rigorous conceptual framework and survey paper, contributing clear formal definitions, well-specified decision-theoretic models, explicit constraints on authorization and risk, and an insightful meta-evaluation schema for future empirical benchmarks.
primary.scoped_contribution: This review and conceptual framework paper formalizes proactive service agents via an operational definition relative to task instructions, framing intervention as a constrained partially observable sequential decision problem where timing, content, and delivery are jointly evaluated against the option value of silence.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript satisfies all standards for a rigorous conceptual framework and survey paper, contributing clear formal definitions, well-specified decision-theoretic models, explicit constraints on authorization and risk, and an insightful meta-evaluation schema for future empirical benchmarks.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly delineate the limitations of current literature, emphasizing that high failure-prediction or classification F1 does not imply real-world deployment utility, and outlining open challenges regarding counterfactual evaluation, preference drift, and multi-regime protocol harmonization.
